summary: Principled, layer-assigned requirement matrix to push up the stack (Skin IR / OxCalc / OxFml) for richer, robuster skinning

result.north_star: A passive, Excel-faithful calc engine (OxFunc/OxFml/OxCalc) feeds a host projection (DnaTreeCalc) consumed by frame-only skins through a closed intent dispatcher. This requirement set pushes truth UP the stack so skins gain deep, robust reach without ever owning semantics: a stable identity spine, lossless typed projections of facts the engine already derives, atomic id-carrying authoring verbs, a consequence-free speculation/time axis, and a composable governed platform. The ordering principle is push-up-the-stack-first: land the keystone identity and the free typed-vs-stringly conversions, then fan out — and honestly distinguish "expose existing engine truth" from three large unbuilt engine workstreams (per-node value epochs, an addressable candidate-overlay substrate, and a retained revision graph) that the speculation/time/async bands actually require.

tenets.name: Identity is permanent, path is cosmetic
tenets.statement: Every model node is addressed by a stable opaque NodeKey (the engine's existing TreeNodeId), invariant across rename/move; the dotted display_path is a derived label. All projections, deltas, selection, scope, references, view-state, persisted SkinState, history, and collaboration key off NodeKey, never the path. The cutover carries BOTH key and display_path during a transition window rather than a single big-bang break.
tenets.rationale: NodeId IS the dotted path in the IR today, so every rename/move silently orphans selection, scroll, pins, expansion, persisted SkinState, delta addressing, references, and history correlation. The engine already mints a stable TreeNodeId(u64) — so the engine side is expose-existing; the L-effort, schedule-risk work is the breaking IR/host cutover, best de-risked by carrying both key and path transitionally. Stable identity is the single precondition that lets value-diff, deltas, undo-navigation, persistence, multi-select, and collaboration correlate the same entity across two observations. It is the keystone.

tenets.name: Typed and lossless over stringly and flattened
tenets.statement: Every fact the engine already derives crosses the IR boundary intact, as closed exhaustive Rust enums/structs keyed by stable identity — never as String prose to grep, a bare count, or a collapsed Scalar(String) — INCLUDING the write-failure channel (IntentError). Where the engine emits an open taxonomy today (phase-timing keys), the IR uses a typed-key map with an explicit Other(String) escape rather than host-side re-classification into invented closed fields. The projection is where engine variants become host enums; the skin matches variants and never re-derives, re-parses, or re-classifies.
tenets.rationale: Invalidation reasons/dependency kinds/IntentError are String, runtime effects/derivation traces are bare counts, tables expose no cells, scalars are raw debug text. A skin forced to grep prose re-implements engine semantics it cannot own, breaks on rewording, and cannot localize. Critically the engine itself still branches on diagnostic prose (e.g. matching 'cycle.excel_match_iterative'); the typed contract is partly aspirational and carries a real engine cleanup obligation. Typing the failure channel is not optional polish — a stringly IntentError is a tenet violation hiding inside the receipt.

tenets.name: Engine is the sole source of derivation, value, and format
tenets.statement: Explanations, traces, caches, schedules, overlays, cycle terminals, conditional-format results, number-format meaning, and rendered value text are READ from the engine that produced them, never reconstructed host- or skin-side. The format/value resolver on SkinContext is a thin forward into OxFml's renderer (it MUST NOT parse or interpret number-format codes host-side); the host attaches only frame concerns (align/color mapped to tokens). 'Formats describe the value; skins describe the frame.'
tenets.rationale: Re-deriving any engine fact host-side risks divergence from Excel-canonical truth (HARD CONSTRAINT 4/7). A host resolver that interpreted format codes itself would re-implement OxFml semantics and reintroduce divergence; constraining it to a forwarding FFI makes constraint-7 a structural guarantee, not a convention. 'Expose-existing' is the dominant readiness for reads — but only where the engine has committed to a closed taxonomy; phase-timing keys and per-edge cache outcomes have NOT, so those are extend-existing pending an engine commitment.

tenets.name: Conceivable is one intent; subjects are first-class, text is the engine's
tenets.statement: Every articulable model change is exactly ONE entry in the closed WorkspaceIntent enum, applied to a typed host-owned SUBJECT (one node, an ordered multi-selection, a subtree, a reference collection) carried in the intent — never a skin-stitched sequence and never synthesized formula text. Fill, F4, paste-formula, column-formula, and reference building all travel as ids/handles; OxFml recomposes RAW text and OxCalc rebinds. Edit-buffer concerns (caret position) stay host-side; OxFml returns composed text the host splices.
tenets.rationale: HARD CONSTRAINTS 1, 2, 3. A skin that fakes a missing op reintroduces formula authoring, partial-failure states, and breakage across profiles/named-refs/moves. Authoring richness scales with subject richness, not verb count. Pushing caret state into an OxFml intent would be the opposite ownership leak — the engine taking on host editing-buffer state it should not model.

tenets.name: All-or-nothing, reversible only by navigation
tenets.statement: A single conceptual edit — even spanning many nodes — commits atomically as ONE transaction producing ONE published revision and ONE projection update, or not at all; its undo is achieved by navigating OxCalc's retained immutable revision GRAPH, never by replaying inverse intents. Every receipt carries the transaction id and produced revision; on failure it reports WHICH scoped edit failed and why (typed).
tenets.rationale: HARD CONSTRAINT 6 plus the synchronous full-republish contract. The engine today publishes PER-NODE and retains only snapshot-IDENTITY hashes, not a navigable revision store — so both atomic-multi-edit transactions AND undo-by-navigation are genuine engine workstreams (new-capability), not expose-existing. Inverse-intent replay is unsound against runtime overlays/spill. The transaction id is the stable correlation handle between the closed-enum layer and revision retention.

tenets.name: Speculation is consequence-free, composable, and provenanced
tenets.statement: Every what-if, scenario, goal-seek, and sweep runs on handle-addressed candidate overlays that are structurally incapable of touching the published revision stream; overlays compose and stack; published value_epoch advances only on an explicit Commit intent. Every projected value is tagged with provenance (Published | Pending | Speculative{handle} | Scenario{id} | External{source}) so a ghost can never be mistaken for real.
tenets.rationale: HARD CONSTRAINT 6/7. The engine today has a per-NODE publish lifecycle and a SINGLE runtime-overlay set pinned to the publication snapshot — NOT 'N addressable layerable non-publishing contexts.' Generalizing it is the largest single engine workstream in this set (new-capability, not extend-existing); the entire band is gated on that one milestone. A provenance discriminator is the only thing preventing a user from trusting an uncommitted number.

tenets.name: Predict before you pay
tenets.statement: Any consequential intent is answerable in the interrogative mood before the imperative: the same dispatcher that mutates can report — without mutating — what an intent WOULD invalidate, collide with, rebind, orphan, cost, and reject. Legality, blast-radius, reference-impact, and drop-validity are first-class pure queries. The host computes ONLY the host-owned fields (collisions, orphans, scope expansion); profile-legality and rebind impact are DELEGATED to engine dry-bind / plan-invalidation and surfaced verbatim.
tenets.rationale: The skin owns no semantics and cannot judge collision/rebind/profile-legality. A host-layer query that returned profile_violations as if it owned them would duplicate engine truth and diverge the moment the engine's gate changes. The invalidation/blast-radius walk uses the EXISTING committed dependency graph and needs NO speculation substrate — so the plan-preview read path must stand alone and must NOT back-edge into the candidate-overlay band.

tenets.name: The frame is composable, negotiated, and presentation-tokened
tenets.statement: Multiple skins mount simultaneously into distinct slots sharing one workspace/selection/shared-state source of truth with defined focus arbitration, keybinding arbitration, and per-slot fault isolation; each skin declares a capability manifest the host negotiates at mount; all visual/locale/accessibility presentation flows through typed tokens on SkinContext. SkinState is the skin's private, schema-versioned, migratable, gc'd possession; shared state is a small AUDITED common ground — and the one calc-affecting shared field (recalc_mode) is treated as dispatcher-level policy, not a raw shared write.
tenets.rationale: The shell mounts ONE skin; theme is hardcoded hex; no a11y/i18n/negotiation/persistence/keybinding-arbitration exercised. The FLOW multi-pane vision and third-party/reviewer extensibility need composition + negotiation + isolation as platform guarantees. recalc_mode changes what the engine does, so leaving its switch as a raw shared write — even audited — lets a skin alter calc behavior outside the closed chokepoint.

tenets.name: Every interaction is observable, governed, and replayable
tenets.statement: Mutation funnels through one dispatcher chokepoint that enforces persona/permission PER INTENT ORIGIN (local or peer), records the (intent, receipt, delta, revision) stream as a deterministic replayable log, and emits minimal addressable projection deltas (sequence-stamped, gap-detecting) alongside the full snapshot. Long calc moves to a HOST-OWNED worker (the engine stays single-threaded and passive; the host pumps bounded calc slices and observes a Pending run-state) — the frame never blocks, polls, or owns scheduling semantics. Frame cost itself is observable.
tenets.rationale: There are no intent-log/replay/permission/delta/async hooks. For a passive + closed-intent + republish architecture the intent stream IS the behavior. Delta-over-republish is the #1 zippiness ceiling. Crucially, 'engine computes off-thread' and 'host drives every tick' cannot both hold — we resolve it by keeping the engine synchronous and making concurrency a HOST concern, so passivity is preserved literally. A '60fps on 100k nodes' goal is unfalsifiable without frame telemetry to attribute a stall to engine-calc vs delta-apply vs render.

requirements.title: Re-key the IR off the engine's stable NodeKey; display_path becomes derived
requirements.principle: Identity is permanent, path is cosmetic
requirements.shape: NodeView { key: NodeKey, display_path: NodeId, .. } where NodeKey wraps the engine's existing oxcalc_core TreeNodeId(u64). WorkspaceState keys node_order, dependencies, selection, scope, references, history, SkinState by NodeKey. TRANSITION WINDOW: carry both key and display_path; intents accept either during migration, then cut over.
requirements.unlocks: Selection, scroll anchor, pins, expansion, persisted SkinState, delta addressing, reference maps, multi-select, value-diff, and history survive rename/move instead of resetting. Precondition for incremental deltas, undo-navigation, persistence, and collaboration.
requirements.doctrinal_note: CRITIQUE FIX (1-minor, 3-minor): the engine ALREADY mints and round-trips a stable TreeNodeId — engine side is expose-existing, NOT L engine work. The L/schedule-risk is the breaking IR/host cutover (every projection field, intent payload, SkinState, walking_skeleton test). De-risk via a transition window carrying both identifiers rather than a big-bang break. Primary ownership is therefore SkinIR-contract/Host-projection, with an OxCalc expose-existing dependency that is essentially done.

requirements.title: Typed invalidation reason & calc-transition enums
requirements.principle: Typed and lossless over stringly and flattened
requirements.shape: enum InvalidationReason { UpstreamValueChanged{source:NodeKey}, StructuralRebindRequired, RefTargetMoved{handle:RefHandle}, CollectionMembershipChanged{family:CollectionId}, OverlayApplied, ManualDirty, CycleParticipant, FormatRuleChanged, .. #[non_exhaustive] }; invalidated_nodes[].reasons: Vec<InvalidationReason> replaces Vec<String>.
requirements.unlocks: Calc X-ray renders reason chips per node and filters 'show only structurally-rebound nodes'; skin matches variants instead of grepping prose, enabling i18n and compiler-checked completeness.
requirements.doctrinal_note: OxCalc already classifies why it invalidated each node to decide rebind; the String is a lossy render of an internal enum. Independent, parallelizable, low-risk expose-existing conversion — schedulable anytime, does not gate on NodeKey for its own shape (reasons referencing source nodes use NodeKey once it lands).

requirements.title: Typed dependency-descriptor kind & carrier enums
requirements.principle: Typed and lossless over stringly and flattened
requirements.shape: enum DependencyKind { DirectRef, QualifiedSibling, CollectionMember, RangeCarrier, NameRef, ExternalAlias, RuntimeSpill, .. #[non_exhaustive] }; enum CarrierDetail { SingleCell, Collection{family:CollectionId,members:u32}, Region{rows:u32,cols:u32}, .. }; descriptors_by_owner[] use these instead of kind:String/carrier_detail:String.
requirements.unlocks: Dependency inspector groups/filters edges by typed kind; precedents/dependents overlay color-codes by kind; find-references scopes by reference family.
requirements.doctrinal_note: The dependency graph is OxCalc-owned; kind/carrier are already discriminated internally to drive rebind-on-structural-change. Independent free conversion; do it anytime.

requirements.title: Typed NodeValueProjection variants
requirements.principle: Typed and lossless over stringly and flattened
requirements.shape: enum NodeValueProjection { Unevaluated, Pending, Empty, Number{raw:f64,unit:Option<UnitHint>}, Text(String), Logical(bool), ErrorV(ExcelError), Array{dims:(u32,u32),cells:Vec<Vec<NodeValueProjection>>}, Reference(RefValue), Lambda{arity:u8,params:Vec<String>}, Rich(RichValueRef), Image(ImageRef) } where RefValue = Single(RefHandle)|Collection{family,members}.
requirements.unlocks: Skin renders numbers right-aligned, logicals as checkboxes, errors with typed glyphs, lambdas with arity badges, references as chips, Empty distinct from Unevaluated — without parsing the debug string. Number.unit feeds unit-aware/chart skins.
requirements.doctrinal_note: EvalValue is OxFunc's value universe; the single Scalar(String) collapses it. Host-projection must NOT add display formatting here (that is the resolver's job, constraint 9). Independent free conversion. unit:Option<UnitHint> is expose-existing IF EvalValue carries a unit/semantic hint; otherwise that field is omitted until it does.

requirements.title: Close run/calc_state enums AND retire engine control-flow-via-diagnostic-string
requirements.principle: Typed and lossless over stringly and flattened
requirements.shape: Keep calc_state:CalcState and last_run.run_state:RunState as closed #[non_exhaustive] enums; designate diagnostics:Vec<String> as the ONLY free-text channel, advisory/non-load-bearing. ENGINE CLEANUP: retire existing sites that branch on diagnostic prose (e.g. matching 'cycle.excel_match_iterative', parsing 'oxfml_reject:{code}') — promote those facts to typed enum fields.
requirements.unlocks: Skins safely switch on lifecycle state for badges and the calc-status bar; the engine stops keying control flow off its own prose, so 'diagnostics are advisory' becomes true rather than aspirational.
requirements.doctrinal_note: CRITIQUE FIX (1-minor): the live engine TODAY leaks control-relevant facts into diagnostics and branches on them downstream — declaring diagnostics non-load-bearing is contradicted by current behavior. This is not n/a: it is OxCalc extend-existing engine debt to retire, otherwise the tenet ships violated on day one.

requirements.title: Per-node published-value epoch stamp (engine bookkeeping)
requirements.principle: Identity is permanent, path is cosmetic
requirements.shape: OxCalc stamps each node's published value with a value_epoch distinct from its input_epoch; NodeView.computed_value pairs with value_epoch:u64. Skin memoizes rendered cells keyed by (NodeKey, value_epoch). If true per-node value epochs prove too costly, the delta channel falls back to workspace value_epoch + the engine's existing invalidated-node set.
requirements.unlocks: Precondition for shape-diff, history scrubbing, delta value carriage, and 'is this stale relative to epoch N'. Lets a skin skip re-formatting unchanged cells at scale.
requirements.doctrinal_note: CRITIQUE FIX (1-minor, 3-blocking): the engine exposes a SINGLE workspace-scope value_epoch and a per-node INPUT epoch (not a published-VALUE epoch). Threading a true per-node value epoch is engine bookkeeping = extend-existing (plausibly new-capability), NOT a host expose-existing thread-through. Resolve the open_question before relying on per-node granularity; the fallback keeps the delta channel unblocked.

requirements.title: Typed-KEY phase-timing map with Other(String) escape
requirements.principle: Typed and lossless over stringly and flattened
requirements.shape: last_run.phase_timings: BTreeMap<PhaseKey, u64> where enum PhaseKey { Invalidate, Schedule, Evaluate, Publish, Overlay, .. Other(String) } is OxCalc-OWNED. Replaces the raw BTreeMap<String,u128>.
requirements.unlocks: Calc X-ray performance lane labels known phases; unknown ad-hoc phases survive via Other(String) instead of being dropped or re-classified; regression detection per phase.
requirements.doctrinal_note: CRITIQUE FIX (1-major): the engine records phases by FREE-STRING keys with ad-hoc names. A fixed 5-field struct would be host RE-CLASSIFICATION of engine prose (the exact anti-pattern) or would silently drop phases. The fix is an engine-owned PhaseKey enum with Other(String) escape — so owner is OxCalc, readiness extend-existing (engine must commit to the enum first).

requirements.title: Explicit runtime-effects list (not just count)
requirements.principle: Typed and lossless over stringly and flattened
requirements.shape: last_run.runtime_effects: Vec<RuntimeEffect> where enum RuntimeEffect { Spill{origin:NodeKey,dims:(u32,u32)}, DynamicRef{owner:NodeKey,resolved:RefHandle}, OverlayWrite{node:NodeKey}, RegionResize{node:NodeKey,from:(u32,u32),to:(u32,u32)} } replaces runtime_effect_count.
requirements.unlocks: FLOW's runtime-effect panel lists exactly what spilled/resolved this tick; array unfurl knows which node spilled and its new dims; overlay debugging shows overwritten nodes.
requirements.doctrinal_note: OxCalc tracks each runtime effect to apply it (the typed RuntimeEffect record genuinely exists); the count is a lossy summary. Honest expose-existing.

requirements.title: Region/spill overlay resize deltas
requirements.principle: Typed and lossless over stringly and flattened
requirements.shape: last_run.overlay_deltas: Vec<OverlayDelta { node:NodeKey, kind:SpillOverlayKind, prior_dims:Option<(u32,u32)>, new_dims:(u32,u32), grew:bool }> alongside runtime_overlay_count.
requirements.unlocks: Array unfurl animates only the changed region; a spill that shrinks/grows highlights reclaimed/overwritten area; FLOW shows 'this spill grew from 3x1 to 5x1'.
requirements.doctrinal_note: Overlay sizing is OxCalc runtime-overlay substrate; the delta is computed internally to apply/clear overlays. No grid/coords — delta is dims+node, not A1 (constraint 3).

requirements.title: Per-edge value-cache hit/miss + scheduling-mode + reuse ratio
requirements.principle: Engine is the sole source of derivation, value, and format
requirements.shape: last_run.scheduling: SchedulingReport { mode:ScheduleMode, edges:Vec<EdgeEval{owner:NodeKey, cache:CacheOutcome(Hit|Miss|Bypassed), reused:bool}>, reuse_ratio:f32 } — CONTINGENT on the scheduler exposing per-edge outcomes.
requirements.unlocks: Calc X-ray's performance lane shows which subtree recomputed vs reused; perf debugging of 'why did this recalc' without guessing.
requirements.doctrinal_note: CRITIQUE FIX (1-major): only an edge-value-cache BASIS fingerprint is confirmed in the engine; per-edge Hit/Miss/Bypassed is NOT confirmed. Downgraded to extend-existing pending confirmation (see open_questions). Do not claim expose-existing until the per-edge record exists.

requirements.title: Full derivation-trace payload + EvaluateFragment read
requirements.principle: Engine is the sole source of derivation, value, and format
requirements.shape: last_run.derivation_traces: Vec<DerivationTrace { node:NodeKey, template:Option<TemplateRef>, hole_bindings:Vec<(HoleId,RefHandle)>, child_calls:Vec<PreparedCall{kernel:String, arg_values:Vec<NodeValueProjection>, result:NodeValueProjection}> }> replaces derivation_trace_count; plus read-only EvaluateFragment(node, sub_expr_id)->NodeValueProjection.
requirements.unlocks: FLOW's explain-stack renders the full ordered child prepared-call tree with per-call kernel inputs/outputs — the most-cited Band A need; formula step-through; hover-a-subexpression-see-its-value.
requirements.doctrinal_note: OxFml/OxCalc build the prepared-call tree to evaluate (the typed DerivationTraceRecord genuinely exists); the count discards it. EvaluateFragment is a read-only single-node re-eval the engine already supports. Honest expose-existing.

requirements.title: Typed cycle diagnostics
requirements.principle: Typed and lossless over stringly and flattened
requirements.shape: dependencies.cycle_groups[].diagnostics: CycleDiagnostic { members:Vec<NodeKey>, profile:IterationProfile, iteration_trace:Vec<IterStep{epoch:u32, max_change:f64}>, terminal:CycleTerminalState(Converged|MaxIter|Diverged), reject_kind:Option<RejectKind> }.
requirements.unlocks: Cycle panel shows convergence curve, terminal state, reject reason instead of an opaque CycleBlocked badge.
requirements.doctrinal_note: CRITIQUE FIX (1-major): the iterative-cycle path is FIXTURE-surfaced — per-iteration max_change exists only for specific hardcoded scenarios, not a general solver over arbitrary cycles. Downgraded to extend-existing; the typed shape is sound but general per-iteration convergence data is not yet engine-derived for arbitrary cycles.

requirements.title: Reference-token to target resolution map (+ reverse index)
requirements.principle: Identity is permanent, path is cosmetic
requirements.shape: WorkspaceState.dependencies += resolution_map: BTreeMap<SourceReferenceHandle, ResolvedRef { token_span:(u16,u16), target:RefTarget(Node(NodeKey)|Collection(CollectionId)|External(AliasId)|Unresolved), collection_members:Option<Vec<NodeKey>> }> plus a reverse index for find-references.
requirements.unlocks: Jump-to-definition / find-references in the formula bar; hover-a-token-highlight-its-target; precedents overlay maps tokens to nodes; powers legality preview's rebind_impact; F4-toggle UI targets the right handle.
requirements.doctrinal_note: OxFml binds tokens to handles and OxCalc resolves handles to targets — both engine-owned; descriptors already carry source_reference_handle. Skin reads for navigation and NEVER parses formula text (constraint 1).

requirements.title: Typed binding/parse diagnostics per node (incl. profile-rejection)
requirements.principle: Typed and lossless over stringly and flattened
requirements.shape: enum BindingDiagnostic { UnresolvedRef{token_span:(u16,u16)}, ProfileRejected{feature:ProfileFeature}, AmbiguousName{name:String}, TypeMismatch, RebindPending }; carried on NodeView and ActiveNodeDetail. ProfileFeature is a readable enum so the UI can explain WHY input is rejected.
requirements.unlocks: Inline red-squiggle authoring feedback at a token span; profile-gating UI explains 'this function is rejected under strict-excel'; X-ray shows nodes needing rebind.
requirements.doctrinal_note: OxFml produces bind diagnostics at parse/bind; profile gating happens there (constraint 5). Owner is OxFml (it emits them); skin renders, never re-validates.

requirements.title: Per-node effective format + per-cell conditional-format RESULT
requirements.principle: Engine is the sole source of derivation, value, and format
requirements.shape: NodeView.effective_format: EffectiveFormat { number_code:String, font, fill, align, .. }; NodeView.cf_results: Vec<CfResult { rule_id:CfRuleId, matched:bool, applied:FormatOverride }>; for arrays, per-cell CfResult indexed by logical cell. READ of evaluated results only.
requirements.unlocks: Skin shows resolved format and which CF rule fired per cell; FLOW's format lens; 'why is this cell red'. Feeds the resolver. Also surfaces validation_state (read).
requirements.doctrinal_note: CF rule semantics are OxFml-owned and already evaluated to decide formatting; the result is engine truth. Host surfaces the evaluated result, never re-evaluates rules host-side (constraint 7). This READ projection is justified independent of any WRITE authoring of CF/validation rules.

requirements.title: Format/value resolver (thin OxFml forward) + profile on SkinContext
requirements.principle: Engine is the sole source of derivation, value, and format
requirements.shape: SkinContext gains profile:CapabilityProfile and resolver:&FormatResolver where resolve() FORWARDS to an OxFml render(value, format_code, locale)->RenderedCell and the host only attaches frame concerns (align/color mapped to tokens). Profile's gated feature set is READABLE so UI can explain rejections.
requirements.unlocks: Every skin renders Excel-faithful display text by calling resolve() instead of debug Scalar text (closes constraint 9); profile-aware input gating UI; localized number/date display via the engine, not the skin.
requirements.doctrinal_note: CRITIQUE FIX (1-minor): a host resolver that PARSED number-format codes would re-implement OxFml semantics and risk divergence (constraint 7). Constrained to a thin forward into OxFml's renderer — the resolver MUST NOT interpret format codes host-side. extend-existing because OxFml must expose a render entrypoint.

requirements.title: First-class active-node / formula-bar detail struct
requirements.principle: Typed and lossless over stringly and flattened
requirements.shape: WorkspaceState.active_detail: Option<ActiveNodeDetail { node:NodeKey, content_text:String, value:NodeValueProjection, effective_format:EffectiveFormat, binding_diagnostics:Vec<BindingDiagnostic>, reference_map:Vec<ResolvedRef> }> derived from selection.primary.
requirements.unlocks: A formula bar / inspector renders the selected node's content + live binding diagnostics + format + reference chips from ONE struct instead of cross-joining nodes/dependencies/diagnostics manually.
requirements.doctrinal_note: Pure projection convenience: a denormalized read view over facts the engine already exposes, keyed by selection. Reduces skin-side re-derivation.

requirements.title: RichValue / Image value handles in projection
requirements.principle: Typed and lossless over stringly and flattened
requirements.shape: NodeValueProjection::Rich(RichValueRef { type_id, fields:Vec<(String,NodeValueProjection)> }) and ::Image(ImageRef { source, alt }); references opaque, resolved via context, not inlined bytes.
requirements.unlocks: Skins render linked-data rich values (stocks/geography) and in-cell images Excel-faithfully; future card-view skins read structured fields without parsing.
requirements.doctrinal_note: RichValue/Image are part of OxFunc's value universe; opaque handles keep the engine the source and avoid host transcoding. Cheap once richer-typed-value lands.

requirements.title: Read-only table cell/column projection
requirements.principle: Typed and lossless over stringly and flattened
requirements.shape: TableProjection gains optional cells_view: fn(table_id)->TableCells { columns:Vec<ColumnView{name, formula:Option<String>, effective_format}>, rows:Vec<Vec<NodeValueProjection>> } — read-only, lazily fetched, NOT the structural intent surface.
requirements.unlocks: A table skin renders actual cell values/column formulas (today TableProjection has identity+counts but NO cells); FLOW's table lens; verifying computed table output against Excel.
requirements.doctrinal_note: Table cells are engine-evaluated values bound to nodes; READ surface only (structural ops are separate intents). Multi-value stays as a node's Array/collection — the table is a node-rooted structured value, not A1 coords (constraint 3).

requirements.title: First-class multi-selection subject (anchor + ordered set)
requirements.principle: Conceivable is one intent; subjects are first-class, text is the engine's
requirements.shape: struct SelectionState { primary:Option<NodeKey>, anchor:Option<NodeKey>, selected:Vec<NodeKey> /*ordered, de-duped*/ }; WorkspaceIntent::SelectNodes(Vec<NodeKey>), ::SelectRange{anchor:NodeKey,focus:NodeKey}, ::ToggleNodeInSelection(NodeKey).
requirements.unlocks: Shift/ctrl-click a set of siblings and apply ONE fill/delete/format verb to all; FLOW's batch authoring gestures become a single subject the verbs target.
requirements.doctrinal_note: SelectionState is host-owned projection truth; range resolution uses node_order/depth the host already projects. SelectNode routes to selection signal only (no recalc). Keyed on NodeKey so it survives structural edits.

requirements.title: Typed AuthoringScope carried by mutating intents
requirements.principle: Conceivable is one intent; subjects are first-class, text is the engine's
requirements.shape: enum AuthoringScope { Node(NodeKey), Nodes(Vec<NodeKey>), Subtree(NodeKey), Collection{owner:NodeKey, source_reference_handle:Handle} }; mutating intents take scope:AuthoringScope instead of a bare NodeId.
requirements.unlocks: One verb spans single node, multi-select, subtree, or a reference collection's members — Delete/Replicate/PasteContent/SetFormatProperty work over any subject without verb explosion.
requirements.doctrinal_note: Scope is a host concept (NodeKeys + host-owned collection handle); carries no semantics. Keeps the closed enum small while making subjects rich. A skin cannot safely expand a Subtree scope (membership + meta-invisibility are host/engine truth).

requirements.title: Atomic batch transaction with single publication (engine accumulate-publish-once)
requirements.principle: All-or-nothing, reversible only by navigation
requirements.shape: WorkspaceIntent::EditNodes(Vec<ScopedEdit>) OR host begin_transaction()->TransactionScope { push(intent); commit()->IntentReceipt }; OxCalc accumulates edits, schedules ONCE, republishes ONE WorkspaceState; rollback on any rejection.
requirements.unlocks: A 50-target fill, multi-node format change, or import bulk edit commits as ONE revision and ONE update — no intermediate flicker, no half-applied model on failure. Prerequisite for every multi-target verb and the speculation commit path.
requirements.doctrinal_note: CRITIQUE FIX (3-major): the engine TODAY publishes PER-NODE (produce_candidate -> PublishReady -> publish_and_clear keyed by TreeNodeId). Accumulate-many-edits-then-publish-once is genuine scheduler rework — the highest-RISK foundational item even though effort=L. Flag explicitly as the gating engine milestone for W2 and beyond.

requirements.title: IntentReceipt carries transaction id + produced revision + completion signal + per-edit failure
requirements.principle: All-or-nothing, reversible only by navigation
requirements.shape: struct IntentReceipt { accepted:bool, error:Option<IntentError>, transaction_id:TxnId, produced_revision:Option<RevisionId>, completed_signal:Option<CompletionToken>, delta:WorkspaceDelta, failed_edit_index:Option<usize> }.
requirements.unlocks: A skin correlates an edit with the revision it produced (undo navigation, optimistic UI, time-scrubber labels), awaits completion once async lands, ties a delta-ledger entry to its cause, and on a failed batch knows WHICH ScopedEdit failed.
requirements.doctrinal_note: Host-owned projection of the dispatch outcome; transaction_id/produced_revision reference OxCalc revision identity. completed_signal Option keeps it synchronous today, async-ready later. failed_edit_index closes the transaction-partial-failure gap.

requirements.title: Typed IntentError replacing Rejected(String)
requirements.principle: Typed and lossless over stringly and flattened
requirements.shape: enum IntentError { ProfileRejected{feature:ProfileFeature}, NameCollision{existing:NodeKey}, WouldFormCycle{members:Vec<NodeKey>}, Forbidden{persona:Persona}, Orphans{refs:Vec<NodeKey>}, EngineRejected{revision:Option<RevisionId>, detail:RejectKind}, Unsupported }. Shares reason vocabulary with legality-impact-preview so pre/post-commit errors match.
requirements.unlocks: A skin renders a recoverable, explainable rejection (profile vs collision vs cycle vs forbidden vs engine-internal) instead of grepping a string; the POST-commit failure path gains a typed shape mirroring the PRE-commit preview.
requirements.doctrinal_note: CRITIQUE FIX (2-major/strongest): IntentError is {Unsupported, Rejected(String)} TODAY — a stringly write-failure channel directly violating tenet-2 while everything else is typed. Foundational, sequenced in W2 with transaction-scope, NOT deferred. EngineRejected.detail surfaces the engine's typed RejectKind verbatim.

requirements.title: Command/intent metadata projection
requirements.principle: Conceivable is one intent; subjects are first-class, text is the engine's
requirements.shape: fn command_catalog(&WorkspaceState, &SelectionState) -> Vec<CommandMeta { intent_kind:IntentKind, title:&'static str, shortcut:Option<KeyChord>, effective_binding:Option<KeyChord>, enabled:bool, disabled_reason:Option<DisabledReason> }>.
requirements.unlocks: Command palette and context menus auto-populate with titles, shortcuts, and enablement (greyed 'Delete' when nothing selected); discoverability of the closed intent set; FLOW's action surface.
requirements.doctrinal_note: Enablement is a function of WorkspaceState+selection+legality, computed where the closed dispatcher lives. Host-intent owns the intent set, so it owns enablement metadata; skin reads, dispatches the chosen intent. effective_binding surfaces the keybinding-registry's resolved chord.

requirements.title: ReplicateContent (fill) carrying source + target IDs
requirements.principle: Conceivable is one intent; subjects are first-class, text is the engine's
requirements.shape: WorkspaceIntent::ReplicateContent{ source:NodeKey, targets:AuthoringScope, mode:ReplicateMode (RelativeRefs|AbsoluteRefs|ValuesOnly) }; host forwards to OxFml which recomposes RAW text per target by reference-relative rebind, then OxCalc schedules within one transaction.
requirements.unlocks: Excel-style fill-down/right by NAME: select a formula node + a target column of siblings, replicate with relative refs, engine rebinds each clone under the active profile. FLOW's 'extend this calc across the children' with no skin text-splicing.
requirements.doctrinal_note: HARD CONSTRAINT 1: skins never rewrite formula text. Relative-vs-absolute adjustment is OxFml grammar/bind; host routes ids+mode only. This is the hard reference-rebind machinery that paste-special and duplicate-subtree also need.

requirements.title: ToggleReferenceBinding (F4) by reference handle
requirements.principle: Conceivable is one intent; subjects are first-class, text is the engine's
requirements.shape: WorkspaceIntent::ToggleReferenceBinding{ node:NodeKey, source_reference_handle:Handle, cycle:BindingCycle (Rel->ColAbs->RowAbs->Abs) }; OxFml mutates the binding mode of that one reference token, re-emits RAW text; OxCalc rebinds.
requirements.unlocks: Excel F4 cycling $A$1 / A$1 / $A1 / A1 on the reference under the cursor — an intent carrying the source_reference_handle, never a character edit.
requirements.doctrinal_note: HARD CONSTRAINT 1 explicitly names F4 as MUST-be-intent-carrying-ids. The handle exists on descriptors; write side is OxFml because absolute/relative is a binding-mode property of the parsed reference.

requirements.title: InsertReference: compose profile-correct reference text for a clicked target
requirements.principle: Conceivable is one intent; subjects are first-class, text is the engine's
requirements.shape: OxFml compose_reference(editing_node:NodeKey, target:NodeKey, binding:BindingMode)->RawText; the HOST owns the edit buffer + caret and splices the returned text at its own caret. The intent carries (editing_node, target, binding) only — NO caret.
requirements.unlocks: Click a node while editing a formula to insert a reference to it (Excel point-mode); the skin never synthesizes 'A1'/name text.
requirements.doctrinal_note: CRITIQUE FIX (1-minor): the original shape pushed caret position into an OxFml intent — an ownership leak (engine taking on host edit-buffer state). Corrected: OxFml COMPOSES profile-correct text; the host performs the splice at its own caret. Composition of reference grammar/naming is OxFml's; caret is the host's.

requirements.title: Typed host Clipboard payload (Values|Formula|Format|Subtree)
requirements.principle: Conceivable is one intent; subjects are first-class, text is the engine's
requirements.shape: struct Clipboard { payload:ClipboardPayload (Values(Vec<NodeValueProjection>) | Formula{source:NodeKey} | Format(EffectiveFormat) | Subtree{root:NodeKey}) }; Copy/Cut intents populate it; PasteContent/PasteSubtree consume it. Distinct from OS clipboard text.

requirements.title: PasteContent with Values|Formula|Format modes

requirements.doctrinal_note: CRITIQUE FIX (3-major): retagged L — it requires the SAME hard rebind machinery as replicate-by-id (its dependency), so it is not cheaper than the thing it depends on. Each mode's semantics lives in its owning engine layer; host orchestrates.

requirements.title: DuplicateNode / CopySubtree / PasteSubtree (structural clone)

requirements.title: Host naming/uniqueness policy + RenameStrategy

requirements.title: Default/initial-content policy for AddNode + template instantiation

requirements.title: SetCollectionMembership (authored reference collections)
requirements.principle: Conceivable is one intent; subjects are first-class, text is the engine's
requirements.shape: WorkspaceIntent::SetCollectionMembership{ owner:NodeKey, source_reference_handle:Handle, members:Vec<NodeKey>, order:MemberOrder }; bumps membership_version/order_version.

requirements.doctrinal_note: HARD CONSTRAINT 3: multi-value is a node Array or a reference COLLECTION, never a grid. The collection descriptor is already projected; OxCalc owns membership/order versioning. A skin cannot mutate membership_version.

requirements.title: SetNodeAttributes / SetMeta (engine-visible, revisioned)
requirements.principle: Conceivable is one intent; subjects are first-class, text is the engine's
requirements.shape: WorkspaceIntent::SetMeta{ node:NodeKey, is_meta:bool }, ::SetNodeAttributes{ node:NodeKey, attrs:NodeAttributePatch }.
requirements.unlocks: Mark a subtree meta (scratch/annotation invisible to formulas) or set authored attributes as reviewable, revisioned edits. FLOW's 'this branch is notes, exclude it from calc'.
requirements.doctrinal_note: HARD CONSTRAINT 8: is_meta subtrees are invisible to formulas, so toggling meta changes the dependency graph — MUST be an engine-visible revisioned intent, not a shared-state flag. Host owns the meta concept; OxCalc re-derives dependencies.

requirements.title: SetNote (per-node comment/annotation)
requirements.principle: Conceivable is one intent; subjects are first-class, text is the engine's
requirements.shape: WorkspaceIntent::SetNote{ node:NodeKey, note:Option<NoteContent> }; NodeView gains note:Option<NoteSummary>. May stay allowed for the Reviewer persona.
requirements.unlocks: Authored notes/comments that survive in the model and projection (vs skin-local state lost on reload); reviewer annotations that round-trip to Excel comments.
requirements.doctrinal_note: A note is authored model content (persist, version, round-trip to Excel comments), so it belongs in the host model + intent path — not in SkinState nor SHARED view state.

requirements.title: SetFormatProperty (per-node effective format authoring)
requirements.principle: Engine is the sole source of derivation, value, and format
requirements.shape: WorkspaceIntent::SetFormatProperty{ scope:AuthoringScope, property:FormatProperty (NumberFormatCode|Font|Fill|Border|Alignment) }; OxFml parses/validates the number-format code; host stores the binding; projection surfaces effective_format.

requirements.doctrinal_note: HARD CONSTRAINT 4/7: format-code parsing is OxFml; rendering engine-faithful. Host orchestrates the write and owns where the format binds; the CODE'S MEANING is OxFml's.

requirements.title: AddCfRule / RemoveCfRule / ReorderCfRules (gated on a concrete FLOW use)
requirements.principle: Engine is the sole source of derivation, value, and format
requirements.shape: WorkspaceIntent::AddCfRule{ scope:AuthoringScope, rule:CfRuleSpec }, ::RemoveCfRule{ scope, rule_id }, ::ReorderCfRules{ scope, order:Vec<CfRuleId> }; OxFml owns rule semantics, OxCalc schedules per-cell evaluation.
