Rule order is significant Excel semantics, hence explicit reorder.

requirements.title: Data-validation rule authoring (gated on a concrete FLOW use)
requirements.principle: Engine is the sole source of derivation, value, and format
requirements.shape: WorkspaceIntent::SetDataValidation{ scope:AuthoringScope, rule:Option<ValidationRule (List(Vec<NodeKey>)|NumberRange{min,max}|CustomFormula{text})> }; OxFml binds/evaluates; NodeView.validation_state:Option<ValidationResult> is surfaced (READ) regardless.
requirements.unlocks: Constrain a node's input to a list/range/custom rule, with engine-evaluated pass/fail surfaced for inline UI.
requirements.doctrinal_note: CRITIQUE FIX (3-major): the validation_state READ is kept (in per-node-effective-format); the WRITE authoring is a net-new OxFml surface, DEFERRED to frontier until a concrete use justifies it. Custom-formula constraints are formula text the engine binds (constraint 1); host carries spec, never computes the result (constraint 7).

requirements.title: RebindReferences / AcceptRepair (author-side counterpart to rejection states)
requirements.principle: Conceivable is one intent; subjects are first-class, text is the engine's
requirements.shape: WorkspaceIntent::RebindReferences{ scope:AuthoringScope }, ::AcceptRepair{ scope:AuthoringScope }; drives OxCalc to re-bind/clear RejectedPendingRepair and requires_rebind states in one transaction; receipt reports repaired nodes.
requirements.unlocks: Batch-repair nodes stuck in RejectedPendingRepair / requires_rebind after structural churn or import — the WRITE verb the read-side rejection states implied. FLOW's 'fix all broken references'.
requirements.doctrinal_note: Rebind/repair is OxCalc/OxFml truth (binding + rejection lifecycle); host carries scope only. Distinct from rename/move integrity (automatic) — this is explicit author-driven repair.

requirements.title: Reference-preserving Rename/Move (rebind, never break)
requirements.principle: Conceivable is one intent; subjects are first-class, text is the engine's
requirements.shape: RenameNode/MoveNode dispatch triggers OxCalc reference rebind so dependents follow the node by stable NodeKey; descriptors_by_owner[].requires_rebind_on_structural_change drives it; receipt reports rebound dependents.
requirements.unlocks: Renaming/moving a node updates all name-based references automatically (Excel name-manager parity) so authoring structure never silently breaks formulas. FLOW's freely-reorganize-the-tree stays safe.
requirements.doctrinal_note: The intents exist; the GAP is guaranteed reference integrity. content_text is name-based and refs carry source_reference_handle, so rebind is OxCalc/OxFml truth keyed on stable NodeKey. Host must not rewrite referencing text (constraint 1).

requirements.title: Pre-commit legality + impact: thin host JOIN over engine dry-bind + plan-invalidation
requirements.principle: Predict before you pay
requirements.shape: host preview_intent(&WorkspaceIntent)->MutationImpact { legal:bool, profile_violations:Vec<ProfileFeature> /*from engine dry_bind*/, requires_rebind:Vec<NodeKey> /*from engine plan_invalidation*/, affected_refs:Vec<NodeKey>, orphaned_dependents:Vec<NodeKey> /*host*/, collisions:Vec<NameCollision> /*host*/, blocked_reason:Option<DisabledReason> }; pure, no mutation. Host computes NONE of the semantic fields, only joins them.
requirements.unlocks: A skin disables an illegal Delete, warns 'renaming rebinds 7 dependents', blocks AddNode under strict-excel, powers command-palette enablement and drop-validity — all BEFORE commit.
requirements.doctrinal_note: CRITIQUE FIX (1-major/strongest): the original presented profile_violations/requires_rebind as host-computed — duplicating engine truth. Recast as a thin ORCHESTRATOR: profile_violations DELEGATED to an engine dry_bind (new dep engine-dry-bind), requires_rebind to plan_invalidation, both surfaced verbatim; only collisions/orphans/scope-expansion are genuinely host. Host computes no semantic field.

requirements.title: OxFml dry-bind: profile/bind legality of an unexecuted edit without mutating
requirements.principle: Predict before you pay
requirements.shape: OxFml dry_bind(edit:&PreviewMutation, profile:CapabilityProfile)->BindVerdict { profile_violations:Vec<ProfileFeature>, bind_diagnostics:Vec<BindingDiagnostic>, would_rebind:Vec<NodeKey> } — parse/bind only, no evaluation, no publish.
requirements.unlocks: The semantic half of legality-impact-preview: profile-rejection and bind diagnostics for an intent that has not been applied. Distinct from recalc-plan-preview (which covers invalidation, not bind-time profile rejection).
requirements.doctrinal_note: CRITIQUE FIX (1-major): legality-impact-preview needs an engine bind-check that recalc-plan-preview does NOT provide (invalidation != profile rejection at bind). Profile gating happens at parse/bind (constraint 5), which is OxFml. New engine read entrypoint.

requirements.title: Recalc-PLAN dry-run over the COMMITTED graph: invalidation set + blast radius
requirements.principle: Predict before you pay
requirements.shape: OxCalc plan_invalidation(&self, edits:&[PreviewMutation]) -> InvalidationPlan { invalidated_nodes:Vec<InvalidationEntry>, evaluation_order:Vec<NodeKey>, requires_rebind:Vec<NodeKey>, estimated_node_count, cycle_risk:Vec<CycleGroup> } — walks the EXISTING committed dependency graph WITHOUT evaluating kernels, publishing, or opening a candidate.
requirements.unlocks: FLOW's delta-ledger preview ('this edit touches 14 nodes, forces 2 rebinds, risks a cycle') as a hover BEFORE commit; the blast-radius highlight on the tree.
requirements.doctrinal_note: CRITIQUE FIX (3-blocking/major): the original depended on candidate-overlay-handle (W4) — a W2->W4 back-edge inversion. The invalidation/blast-radius walk uses ONLY the committed dependency graph (reverse edges + rebind flags the engine already computes every tick); it needs NO speculation substrate. Standalone read path so W2 stands on W0/W1 alone.

requirements.title: Drop-legality query + typed drag/drop contract for tree gestures
requirements.principle: Predict before you pay
requirements.shape: host drop_legality(dragged:AuthoringScope, over:NodeKey, position:DropPosition{Before|After|Into})->DropVerdict{ legal:bool, would_rebind:Vec<NodeKey>, would_orphan:Vec<NodeKey>, collision:Option<NameCollision> } reusing legality-impact-preview; SkinIR DropPosition/DropVerdict types. Drag STATE (what is dragged, pointer pos) stays skin-local; only the verdict crosses the boundary.
requirements.unlocks: Live drop-target validity feedback DURING a drag, insertion-point indicators, multi-node drag of a SelectionState set, cross-slot drag (tree node into scenario pane) — consistent across every tree skin.
requirements.doctrinal_note: CRITIQUE FIX (2-major): a tree-centric platform was missing a first-class drag model; FLOW's 'drag-preview gutter' was mentioned but never specified. Gesture state is skin view-state; the legality verdict is the only boundary-crossing fact, reusing the existing preview.

requirements.title: Model search/filter query projection
requirements.principle: Every interaction is observable, governed, and replayable
requirements.shape: query(QuerySpec{ text_match:Option<String>, calc_state_filter:Option<CalcState>, has_error:bool, references:Option<NodeKey>, is_meta:Option<bool> })->QueryResult{ matches:Vec<NodeKey>, total }. Pure read over node_order + nodes + reverse_edges.
requirements.unlocks: FIND a node in a 100k-node tree: name/content search, 'show only nodes with errors', 'nodes referencing X', go-to-node; pairs with virtualization (a window anchored on a match). Without it, virtualization can only scroll, never jump.
requirements.doctrinal_note: CRITIQUE FIX (2-major): search/filter was an absent domain that makes virtualization usable. Distinct from find-references (token-level) — this is whole-model node search. Results keyed by NodeKey survive edits.

requirements.title: Template author/instantiate/sync/detach intents + template_index
requirements.principle: Conceivable is one intent; subjects are first-class, text is the engine's
requirements.shape: WorkspaceIntent::PromoteToTemplate{ source:NodeKey, name }, ::InstantiateTemplate{ template_id, parent, bindings }, ::EditTemplate{..}, ::SyncInstance{ instance }, ::DetachInstance{ instance }; WorkspaceState gains template_index + NodeView.instance_of/drift.
requirements.unlocks: Reusable model templates with managed instances and drift tracking — FLOW's 'define a department block once, stamp it per region, push edits to all instances.'
requirements.doctrinal_note: Templates are explicitly host-owned. Instantiation reuses the clone/rebind path (OxFml/OxCalc for internal refs); host owns template identity, instance->template link, and drift detection.

requirements.title: Table Insert/Delete Row|Column + SetColumnFormula
requirements.principle: Conceivable is one intent; subjects are first-class, text is the engine's
requirements.shape: WorkspaceIntent::InsertTableRow{table,at}, ::DeleteTableRow{table,at}, ::InsertTableColumn{table,at,spec}, ::DeleteTableColumn{table,at}, ::SetColumnFormula{table,column,source_reference_handle}; TableProjection gains columns metadata (still NO grid coords).
requirements.unlocks: Authoring structured tables: add/remove rows/columns and set a calculated-column formula that fills the column by reference (engine rebinds per row).
requirements.doctrinal_note: HARD CONSTRAINT 3: no grid/coords — these are structural (row/column as table structure, not cell addresses); SetColumnFormula is reference-relative fill owned by OxFml/OxCalc. Confirm the engine's table notion reconciles rows+columns without reintroducing 2D coordinate addressing (open_question).

requirements.title: RegisterAlias / UnregisterAlias + alias manifest projection
requirements.principle: Conceivable is one intent; subjects are first-class, text is the engine's
requirements.shape: WorkspaceIntent::RegisterAlias{ local_name, target_workspace, target_node:NodeKey }, ::UnregisterAlias{ local_name }; WorkspaceState gains alias_manifest + per-descriptor external_available:bool.
requirements.unlocks: Referencing another workspace's node by a stable local alias, engine tracking external availability/staleness. FLOW's cross-model links.
requirements.doctrinal_note: Cross-workspace resolution + external-availability are scheduling/dependency truth (OxCalc owns the dep graph across revisions). Host registers the alias and projects the manifest; cannot judge external availability. Aliases keep refs as ids/handles, never spliced text.

requirements.title: ImportWorkbook dry-run + ImportManifestProjection
requirements.principle: Predict before you pay
requirements.shape: WorkspaceIntent::ImportWorkbook{ source, mode:DryRun|Commit }; DryRun returns ImportManifestProjection{ proposed_nodes, binding_diagnostics, unsupported_features } without mutating; Commit applies in one transaction.
requirements.unlocks: Bringing an existing Excel workbook into the tree model with a preview of what maps cleanly vs needs repair, before committing. FLOW's onboarding from real spreadsheets.
requirements.doctrinal_note: Host owns model<->Excel mapping; parse/bind of imported formulas is OxFml, scheduling OxCalc. Dry-run produces a NON-published manifest, respecting no-partial-publish.

requirements.title: ExportWorkbook (round-trip OUT to Excel) + value-snapshot export
requirements.principle: Conceivable is one intent; subjects are first-class, text is the engine's
requirements.shape: WorkspaceIntent::ExportWorkbook{ scope:AuthoringScope, mode:ExportMode{ValuesOnly|FormulasAndFormat|FullModel} }->ExportArtifact{ format, bytes_handle }; plus a lighter Host-projection value_snapshot(scope)->Csv|Json over computed_value.
requirements.unlocks: Export-to-Excel (backs the canonical-verification loop — comparing against a real workbook), render-to-report, CSV/value snapshot. A platform that imports but cannot export traps user work.
requirements.doctrinal_note: CRITIQUE FIX (2-minor): export was an entirely absent output domain, arguably load-bearing given 'verify against Excel as canonical truth' implies a comparable workbook artifact. Host owns model<->Excel mapping (its stated ownership); formula/format serialization is OxFml. value-snapshot is a lighter read.

requirements.title: Typed numeric/temporal Series projection for chart/visualization skins
requirements.principle: Engine is the sole source of derivation, value, and format
requirements.shape: series(scope:AuthoringScope | reference-collection)->Series{ points:Vec<(label:String, NodeValueProjection)>, unit:Option<UnitHint> } — resolves a scope into a plottable series without re-walking the tree.
requirements.unlocks: A chart/value-board skin reads a time-series or numeric series off the tree in a plottable shape; pairs with comparative-multi-overlay-projection to feed tornado/spider charts from a sweep grid.
requirements.doctrinal_note: CRITIQUE FIX (2-minor): sensitivity sweeps and comparative columns produced chart DATA but nothing specified how a chart skin consumes it. A shaped READ over engine-rendered values; the skin lays them out, the engine owns every value. unit rides on richer-typed-value's UnitHint.

requirements.title: OxCalc retains an addressable immutable revision GRAPH (store + parents + cursor)
requirements.principle: All-or-nothing, reversible only by navigation
requirements.shape: OxCalc retains published revisions in an addressable store: RevisionId -> RetainedRevision { parent:Option<RevisionId>, value_epoch, edit_transaction_id, snapshot_refs }; a navigable cursor; fn revision_at(id), fn navigate(id). A DAG because edit-after-undo branches.
requirements.unlocks: The substrate ALL of undo-navigation, version-history, time-scrubbing, and collaboration depend on. Without it, HARD CONSTRAINT 6 (undo = navigate retained revisions) has no engine to navigate.
requirements.doctrinal_note: CRITIQUE FIX (3-blocking): the engine TODAY holds snapshot-IDENTITY hashes (content hashes for change detection), NOT a retained navigable revision store with parent links — formula.rs even notes 'retained non-table replay missing'. Undo-by-navigation therefore has NO substrate; this is a genuine new-capability engine workstream that MUST precede the time axis. Surfaced as an explicit gating milestone.

requirements.title: Handle-addressed, layerable, non-publishing candidate overlay substrate
requirements.principle: Speculation is consequence-free, composable, and provenanced
requirements.shape: OxCalc: fn open_candidate(basis:RevisionId)->CandidateHandle; fn apply_overlay(h, overlay:OverlaySet); fn evaluate_candidate(h)->CandidateRun; fn close_candidate(h). Candidates layer (a candidate may declare a parent) and NEVER enter the publication queue.
requirements.unlocks: Multiple simultaneous what-ifs / scenario comparisons / sweep points at once; PreviewEdit, scenarios, goal-seek, sensitivity all share ONE substrate. The Band C keystone and the single largest engine risk.
requirements.doctrinal_note: CRITIQUE FIX (3-blocking/strongest): the engine TODAY has a per-NODE publish lifecycle plus a SINGLE RuntimeOverlaySet pinned to the publication snapshot — there is NO open_candidate, no parented/layered candidates, no isolation from the publication queue. Going from one publish path to many isolated parented overlay contexts is scheduler rework = NEW-CAPABILITY, not extend-existing. The whole speculation band is gated on this one milestone.

requirements.title: Published/pending/speculative/scenario/external provenance on every value
requirements.principle: Speculation is consequence-free, composable, and provenanced
requirements.shape: ValueProvenance { origin:Published|Pending|Speculative{handle:SpeculationHandle}|Scenario{scenario_id}|External{source}, basis_epoch:ValueEpoch } carried alongside computed_value on NodeView and in overlay_values maps; plus is_stale:bool during async runs.
requirements.unlocks: Skin renders ghost vs real vs scenario vs external values with unambiguous styling; the delta ledger attributes each row to its source; during async recalc users see dimmed last-good values, not blanks.
requirements.doctrinal_note: SkinIR-contract enrichment adding a discriminator the engine knows (which overlay/source produced the value). Constraint 7 respected: provenance is metadata; the value stays engine-rendered raw.

requirements.title: PreviewEdit / WhatIf intent producing a non-published CalcRunProjection
requirements.principle: Speculation is consequence-free, composable, and provenanced
requirements.shape: WorkspaceIntent::PreviewEdit{ edits:Vec<PreviewMutation>, handle:SpeculationHandle }; receipt carries preview:Option<PreviewProjection { handle, run:CalcRunProjection, overlay_values:BTreeMap<NodeKey,NodeValueProjection>, value_epoch_basis }>. NEVER advances published value_epoch.
requirements.unlocks: FLOW's ghost what-if: typing into a node shows the downstream recompute as a ghost overlay without committing; skin renders provisional style and offers Commit/Discard.
requirements.doctrinal_note: A deliberate closed-enum addition. The candidate evaluation is OxCalc's; host marshals the edit payload. Constraint 1: carries the same raw-text/id payload an EditFormula would; engine rebinds.

requirements.title: Discard / Commit terminal actions for a speculation handle
requirements.principle: Speculation is consequence-free, composable, and provenanced
requirements.shape: WorkspaceIntent::CommitSpeculation{handle} applies the candidate's edits as a normal published edit-transaction (advances value_epoch, becomes a retained revision, returns edit_transaction_id); ::DiscardSpeculation{handle} closes the candidate, no revision created.
requirements.unlocks: The only two terminal actions on a ghost what-if: bless it into history or drop it for free. Makes 'explore freely, commit deliberately' the core FLOW loop.
requirements.doctrinal_note: Commit is the SOLE bridge from speculation to the publish path. Host-intent sequences engine accept + revision retention; engine owns the publication.

requirements.title: Named scenario override set (engine overlay) + scenario intents
requirements.principle: Speculation is consequence-free, composable, and provenanced
requirements.shape: WorkspaceIntent::SetScenarioOverride{scenario_id, node:NodeKey, value:OverrideInput}, ClearScenarioOverride{..}, CreateScenario{name}, DeleteScenario{scenario_id}, ActivateScenario{scenario_id:Option<ScenarioId>}. OverrideInput carries raw content; engine binds it.
requirements.unlocks: FLOW's scenario rail: 'Base/Bull/Bear' tabs each holding input overrides; activating one re-projects the whole tree against that overlay.
requirements.doctrinal_note: Override VALUES live as an OxCalc overlay (they participate in coercion/array-lift/error algebra); naming/active-selection is host projection state. Constraint 1: SetScenarioOverride carries raw text, engine rebinds. Durable round-trip to Excel scenario-manager is an open_question.

requirements.title: Scenario manifest + active-scenario in the read projection
requirements.principle: Speculation is consequence-free, composable, and provenanced
requirements.shape: WorkspaceState += scenarios:ScenarioManifest { entries:Vec<ScenarioEntry{id, name, override_count, overridden_nodes:Vec<NodeKey>, value_epoch}>, active:Option<ScenarioId> }; NodeView += scenario_override:Option<NodeValueProjection> when active scenario overrides it.
requirements.unlocks: Scenario rail UI renders tabs + per-scenario override badges; the delta ledger shows 'this node is overridden in Bear scenario.'
requirements.doctrinal_note: Pure read-projection addition. Manifest metadata host-owned, override values engine-rendered.

requirements.title: Side-by-side multi-overlay value projection (compare N candidates)
requirements.principle: Speculation is consequence-free, composable, and provenanced
requirements.shape: ComparativeProjection { basis:ValueEpoch, columns:Vec<OverlayColumn{label, source:ValueProvenance, values:BTreeMap<NodeKey,NodeValueProjection>}> } — one column per active candidate/scenario, baseline included.
requirements.unlocks: The scenario rail's comparison view and the sensitivity sweep grid: Base | Bull | Bear as adjacent columns per node; no Excel data-table can do this over a tree shape.
requirements.doctrinal_note: A shaped READ over multiple engine candidate handles. Each column's values are engine-rendered; the skin only lays them out.

requirements.title: Value-shape diff keyed by value_epoch (dims + changed-cell mask)
requirements.principle: Predict before you pay
requirements.shape: OxCalc value_delta(from:ValueEpoch, to:ValueEpoch) -> ValueDelta { per_node:BTreeMap<NodeKey, NodeValueDelta { prior_dims:Option<(u32,u32)>, new_dims, changed:ChangeMask, kind_changed:bool }> }; works between any two epochs incl. a candidate's.
requirements.unlocks: FLOW's delta ledger / change-pulse: precisely which nodes/cells changed between baseline and a what-if, as a heat overlay; array deltas show only changed cells.
requirements.doctrinal_note: OxCalc owns value epochs + retained revisions, so it owns the diff. Inherits value-epoch-keying's risk: if only workspace value_epoch + per-node input_epoch exist, true per-node value diff is larger than expose-existing. Mask is logical cells, not grid coords (constraint 3).

requirements.title: Derivation trace addressable per candidate (why-did-this-change)
requirements.principle: Engine is the sole source of derivation, value, and format
requirements.shape: fn derivation_trace(h:CandidateHandle, node:NodeKey) -> DerivationTrace; extends full-derivation-trace addressability from the single published run to any candidate.
requirements.unlocks: In a what-if the user asks 'why is this value different under Bear?' and gets the full kernel-level explanation; pairs with value-shape-diff to explain, not just show.
requirements.doctrinal_note: OxCalc owns the derivation trace; Band C extends its addressability to any candidate so explanation is available off the publish path.

requirements.title: Goal-seek substrate: iterate a candidate to a target
requirements.principle: Speculation is consequence-free, composable, and provenanced
requirements.shape: fn goal_seek(basis:RevisionId, GoalSeekSpec { target_node:NodeKey, target_value:f64, by_node:NodeKey, tolerance, max_iters }) -> GoalSeekResult { converged:bool, solved_value:Option<NodeValueProjection>, iterations:Vec<IterationStep>, terminal:GoalSeekTermination }. Runs entirely inside candidate overlays.
requirements.unlocks: FLOW's goal-seek ('set this output to 1M by varying this input') with a visible convergence trace; each Newton step is a candidate eval that never touches history.
requirements.doctrinal_note: CRITIQUE FIX (1-major): do NOT cite 'already handles cycles/iteration' as readiness — the cycle/iteration path is fixture-surfaced, not a general solver. A Newton/secant goal-seek loop driving candidate evals is genuinely new scheduler work distinct from cycle fixed-point iteration. Gated behind the proven candidate-overlay milestone.

requirements.title: Sensitivity / sweep substrate: N parallel candidate points
requirements.principle: Speculation is consequence-free, composable, and provenanced
requirements.shape: fn sweep(basis:RevisionId, SweepSpec { vary:Vec<SweepAxis{node:NodeKey, points:Vec<OverrideInput>}>, observe:Vec<NodeKey> }) -> SweepResult { grid:Vec<SweepCell { inputs, outputs:BTreeMap<NodeKey,NodeValueProjection>, run_summary }> }. Each grid point is an independent candidate; none publishes.
requirements.unlocks: Sensitivity sweeps no Excel data-table can do: vary tree-shaped inputs across N points, observe multiple outputs, tornado/spider charts off the result grid (via series-projection).
requirements.doctrinal_note: A sweep is many independent candidate evaluations — pure engine work, host-driven (passive). Vary/observe axes are arbitrary tree nodes, not a contiguous grid. Gated behind the candidate milestone.

requirements.title: Speculation lifecycle: lease, budget, GC, orphan reclamation
requirements.principle: Speculation is consequence-free, composable, and provenanced
requirements.shape: Candidate handles carry a lease; fn reap_candidates(policy:ReapPolicy) closes un-pinned/un-referenced candidates past a budget; projection exposes speculation_pressure:SpeculationPressure { open_candidates, retained_revisions, mem_estimate } in last_run/diagnostics.
requirements.unlocks: Lets sweep/goal-seek open hundreds of transient candidates without unbounded memory; the skin shows 'speculation pressure' and the engine reclaims safely.
requirements.doctrinal_note: OxCalc owns candidate/revision memory; pinned views (host) are the GC roots it must honor. Passive: host triggers reap; engine never reaps unilaterally during a host-driven tick.

requirements.title: Pinned / stable speculative views (frozen candidate snapshot)
requirements.principle: Speculation is consequence-free, composable, and provenanced
requirements.shape: Shared-state (audited write): pinned_speculations:Vec<PinnedView { handle:SpeculationHandle, label, basis_epoch }>. A pinned candidate is kept alive (not closed) so its projection stays stable while the user explores other what-ifs.
requirements.unlocks: FLOW's 'keep this what-if on screen while I try another'; the scenario rail can pin Base while editing Bear.
requirements.doctrinal_note: Host-projection/shared state owns view persistence + which candidates stay open. The candidate itself is engine-owned; pinning just defers close_candidate. Must be an audited shared write.

requirements.title: Undo/Redo as OxCalc revision-graph navigation + NavigateRevision intent
requirements.principle: All-or-nothing, reversible only by navigation
requirements.shape: WorkspaceIntent::Undo, ::Redo, ::NavigateRevision{target:RevisionId}; dispatcher moves a revision CURSOR over the retained revision DAG and republishes the WorkspaceState for that snapshot. NEVER synthesizes inverse edits.
requirements.unlocks: Correct, deterministic undo/redo across runtime overlays and spill; FLOW's time-scrubber sliding the workspace to any past revision; substrate for collaboration and what-if branching.
requirements.doctrinal_note: CRITIQUE FIX (3-blocking): retagged new-capability — there is no retained navigable revision store today (see revision-graph-retention). HARD CONSTRAINT 6: undo = navigate retained revisions, NEVER inverse-replay (unsound against overlays). Cannot be scheduled before revision-graph-retention exists.

requirements.title: VersionHistoryProjection over retained revisions (a DAG, not a stack)
requirements.principle: All-or-nothing, reversible only by navigation
requirements.shape: WorkspaceState += history:VersionHistoryProjection { entries:Vec<RevisionEntry { revision_id, value_epoch, edit_transaction_id, label:Option<String>, parent:Option<RevisionId>, is_current:bool, summary:Vec<NodeKey> }>, current:RevisionId }. A DAG, since edit-after-undo branches.
requirements.unlocks: FLOW's time-scrubber rail and history panel: scrub to any revision, see what each edit touched, branch points after undo-then-edit. The temporal axis made visible.
requirements.doctrinal_note: CRITIQUE FIX (3-blocking): retagged new-capability via its dependency on revision-graph-retention. Modeling it as a DAG (not a stack) is required because edit-after-undo forks history; Excel's linear undo cannot express this.

requirements.title: Incremental projection delta alongside full snapshot
requirements.principle: Every interaction is observable, governed, and replayable
requirements.shape: enum WorkspaceDelta { NodesChanged(Vec<NodeKey>), ValuesChanged(Vec<(NodeKey,NodeValueProjection)>), DepsChanged(Vec<NodeKey>), CalcRun(CalcRunProjection), Structural(StructuralDelta), FullReset }; receipt carries delta:WorkspaceDelta and the workspace signal exposes a delta stream alongside the full ReadSignal. Keys on the engine's existing invalidated-node set; uses per-node value_epoch when available else workspace epoch.
requirements.unlocks: Skins re-render only changed rows instead of diffing a full clone — the single biggest responsiveness win; makes spill/region-resize and value-shape-diff cheap; a virtualized tree updates O(changed) not O(model).
requirements.doctrinal_note: CRITIQUE FIX (3-blocking): no longer hard-depends on per-node value_epoch — it keys on the engine's existing invalidated_nodes set, so it is not blocked by value-epoch-keying's risk. The host maps engine invalidation into a delta rather than discarding it via full re-snapshot. Republish stays synchronous and complete; the delta is additive.

requirements.title: Monotonic projection version stamp + delta sequencing guard
requirements.principle: Every interaction is observable, governed, and replayable
requirements.shape: WorkspaceState.projection_seq:u64; each delta carries from_seq->to_seq; a skin that detects a gap requests a full resync.
requirements.unlocks: Correctness guarantee for the incremental path: a dropped/reordered delta is detected and triggers resync instead of corrupting the displayed model.
requirements.doctrinal_note: The sequencing contract is part of the IR (producer host + consumer skin must agree). Cheap insurance that makes 'Delta over Republish' trustworthy.

requirements.title: Host-owned worker calc with Pending run-state (engine stays synchronous/passive)
requirements.principle: Every interaction is observable, governed, and replayable
requirements.shape: The HOST runs the synchronous engine calc on a worker, pumping bounded slices per tick; CalcRunProjection.run_state gains Pending { token:RunToken, started_value_epoch }; dispatch returns immediately with completion:Option<CompletionToken>; host republishes (or deltas) on the completion tick. The skin renders run_state; never owns threading.
requirements.unlocks: A slow recalc on a large model no longer freezes the frame; skins dim stale values and show progress while staying interactive. Foundation for external value motion and time-taking speculation.
requirements.doctrinal_note: CRITIQUE FIX (1-major, 3-major/strongest): 'engine computes off-thread' and 'host drives every tick' cannot both hold. RESOLVED by choosing model (A): the engine stays SINGLE-THREADED and passive; concurrency is a HOST concern (host owns the worker, pumps slices, observes Pending). So owner is Host-projection and the calc itself is engine n/a — there is no engine threading new-capability. This removes the latent contradiction.

requirements.title: Intent coalescing + backpressure for rapid edits during async calc
requirements.principle: Every interaction is observable, governed, and replayable
requirements.shape: Dispatcher coalesces superseded edits (successive EditContentDeferred on same NodeKey) and drops/queues recalc requests while a run is Pending; receipt may return Coalesced { into_seq }.
requirements.unlocks: Typing fast or dragging a slider doesn't queue 50 full recalcs; the engine sees the latest intent. Keeps the UI responsive under input pressure.
requirements.doctrinal_note: Coalescing is a host scheduling concern over the intent stream; it must preserve observable correctness (final state == as if all applied in order). EditContentDeferred already signals coalescible intent.

requirements.title: Frame-cost telemetry: dispatch-to-paint latency per intent
requirements.principle: Every interaction is observable, governed, and replayable
requirements.shape: skin-framework instrumentation emitting FrameMetric{ intent_seq, dispatch_to_delta_us, delta_apply_us, render_us, dropped:bool } into the same sink as intent-log-replay; SkinContext gains an optional metrics tap.
requirements.unlocks: Attribute a stall to engine-calc vs delta-apply vs skin-render; makes the '60fps on 100k nodes' target falsifiable; correlates frame cost to its causing intent.
requirements.doctrinal_note: CRITIQUE FIX (2-minor): the matrix had rich engine telemetry but nothing measuring the FRAME, making the performance-budget tenet unfalsifiable. Frame instrumentation is a skin-framework concern; correlates to the causing intent via seq.

requirements.title: Windowed/range projection request for virtualized large trees
requirements.principle: Every interaction is observable, governed, and replayable
requirements.shape: request_window(WindowSpec { anchor:NodeKey, before, after, expanded_set })->only the NodeViews in view + their values; off-window nodes reference-only. Pairs with the delta channel for scroll and with model-query for jump-to-match.
requirements.unlocks: A 100k-node model renders only the ~100 visible rows; scrolling fetches a new window. Essential for very large models.
requirements.doctrinal_note: Windowing is a host projection-shaping concern; the engine holds all nodes, the host decides which to materialize. Must stay consistent under deltas; an off-window delta updates the reference, not a full view.

requirements.title: Wire RightInspector/SplitLeft/SplitRight mount slots with per-slot context
requirements.principle: The frame is composable, negotiated, and presentation-tokened
requirements.shape: Shell mounts a SlotLayout { main, right_inspector, split_left, split_right }; each slot gets its own SkinContext sharing the SAME workspace + selection + shared signals but distinct typed SkinState; SlotId on context.
requirements.unlocks: The FLOW multi-pane vision: tree in Main, active-node detail in RightInspector, what-if/scenario in a split pane — simultaneously, by independent skins.
requirements.doctrinal_note: Composition is a host/shell concern (the shell owns mounting). Skins remain frame-only. Shared truth via one signal set keeps panes coherent without skins coordinating.

requirements.title: Cross-slot focus + hover + recent-selection arbitration in shared state
requirements.principle: The frame is composable, negotiated, and presentation-tokened
requirements.shape: Shared state gains focused_slot:Option<SlotId>, hovered:Option<NodeKey>, recent_selections:VecDeque<NodeKey> (bounded); arbitration helper so one slot's selection drives others' highlight without focus theft.
requirements.unlocks: Selecting a node in the tree highlights it in the inspector and what-if pane; hover in one pane previews in another; back/forward through visited nodes; FLOW's breadcrumb trail.
requirements.doctrinal_note: Focus/hover/recent-selection are view-coordination state, not model truth — host shared state, keyed on stable NodeKey so they survive structural edits.

requirements.title: Cross-slot keybinding registry with conflict resolution
requirements.principle: The frame is composable, negotiated, and presentation-tokened
requirements.shape: host resolves KeyChord->IntentId per focused_slot with a conflict policy (focused slot wins, then global); user overrides persist in audited SharedState; surfaces effective_bindings in command_catalog.
requirements.unlocks: Two simultaneously-mounted skins both wanting Ctrl+D are arbitrated; user-rebindable, scope-aware (chord means different things per focused_slot); the palette shows the resolved chord.
requirements.doctrinal_note: CRITIQUE FIX (2-minor): with multi-pane composition, keyboard input is an arbitration problem (same gap as shared-focus but for keys) the matrix did not address. Host resolves bindings; conflict policy is host policy.

requirements.title: Typed, audited shared-state writes; recalc_mode treated as dispatcher policy
requirements.principle: Every interaction is observable, governed, and replayable
requirements.shape: Replace direct-mutation shared fields (tree_collapsed, pinned, manual_recalc_pending, active_workspace_id, active_scenario, pinned_speculations) with a SharedStore set(key,value) that validates and records (SlotId, key, prev, next, ts) into a bounded audit ring; typed key enum. The recalc_mode SWITCH (calc-affecting) routes through the dispatcher (or is read as dispatcher-level host policy), NOT a raw shared write.
requirements.unlocks: Debuggable cross-skin interaction; prevents one skin corrupting another's assumptions; replay includes shared-state transitions; closes the side-door mutation gap.
requirements.doctrinal_note: CRITIQUE FIX (1-minor): recalc_mode GATES calc behavior, so leaving its switch as even an audited shared write lets a skin alter calc behavior outside the closed chokepoint — undercutting 'mutation funnels through one dispatcher'. The calc-affecting mode selection is reclassified to dispatcher-level treatment; purely cosmetic view-state stays in the SharedStore.

requirements.title: Exercise SkinState persist + schema-versioned migration + identity-keyed gc
requirements.principle: The frame is composable, negotiated, and presentation-tokened
requirements.shape: Persist each slot's SkinState keyed by (skin_id, slot_id, workspace_id); on load run migrate(from schema_version); run gc(live_node_keys) to drop view-state for deleted nodes. Round-trip tested.
requirements.unlocks: View-state (expansion, pins, column widths, scenarios) survives reload and skin upgrades; renamed nodes keep view-state (gc keys off NodeKey). Makes the dead contract real.
requirements.doctrinal_note: SkinState is the skin's owned, versioned possession; persistence/migration/gc are part of that contract. gc must key off stable NodeKey so renamed nodes keep state, deleted nodes are reclaimed.

requirements.title: Scenario + pinned-view metadata persistence in SkinState (values stay in engine)
requirements.principle: Speculation is consequence-free, composable, and provenanced
requirements.shape: Scenario names/metadata and pinned-view labels persist via SkinState (serde + schema_version + migrate + gc). Override VALUES are NOT persisted in skin state — they round-trip through the engine model.
requirements.unlocks: Scenarios survive reload; FLOW's scenario rail is durable, not session-only.
requirements.doctrinal_note: Only NAMES/metadata persist in skin state; override values persist in the engine model (constraint 4/7 — values are engine-faithful, the skin must not become a parallel value store). Whether the engine has a DURABLE Excel-round-tripping scenario store is an open_question.

requirements.title: Design tokens on SkinContext (CSS vars) with dark + high-contrast
requirements.principle: The frame is composable, negotiated, and presentation-tokened
requirements.shape: SkinContext.tokens:ThemeTokens resolving to CSS custom properties; ThemeMode { Light, Dark, HighContrast }; shell sets the active theme; skins reference var(--surface), var(--space-2), never literal hex.
requirements.unlocks: Dark mode, high-contrast a11y theme, and brand re-skinning apply to EVERY skin at once; removes hardcoded-hex coupling in theme.rs/shell.
requirements.doctrinal_note: Theming is pure frame presentation — skin-layer territory, exposed via SkinContext. Distinct from VALUE formatting (engine-owned resolver). Independent free win.

requirements.title: Accessibility primitives: roving tabindex, ARIA tree roles, active-descendant
requirements.principle: The frame is composable, negotiated, and presentation-tokened
requirements.shape: Skin-framework helpers: tree_a11y(node_key, depth, expanded, selected)->AriaAttrs; roving-tabindex controller bound to the selection signal; aria-activedescendant wired to NodeKey-derived stable DOM ids.
requirements.unlocks: Keyboard navigation, screen-reader support, focus management for every tree/table skin without each author re-implementing it.
requirements.doctrinal_note: A11y is a frame concern; lives in the skin framework as reusable primitives. Stable NodeKey is needed for stable DOM ids that active-descendant references.

requirements.title: Locale/i18n presentation: RTL + UI-string catalog (NOT value formatting)
requirements.principle: The frame is composable, negotiated, and presentation-tokened
requirements.shape: SkinContext.locale:LocaleTokens { dir:Ltr|Rtl, ui_strings:&Catalog }; skins pull chrome labels/tooltips from the catalog and honor dir. Number/date VALUE formatting stays in the engine resolver.
requirements.unlocks: RTL layouts and translated skin chrome without per-skin string surgery; the same skin ships in multiple languages.
requirements.doctrinal_note: Critical boundary: UI-chrome strings + layout direction are FRAME (skin); number/date/currency VALUE formatting is Excel-faithful ENGINE truth and must NOT be re-localized in the skin. Deliberately scoped to chrome only.

requirements.title: Skin capability manifest + host negotiation at mount
requirements.principle: The frame is composable, negotiated, and presentation-tokened
requirements.shape: SkinManifest { required_read_fields, required_intents:Vec<IntentId>, required_slots, min_profile, schema_version }; host negotiate(manifest)->Result<MountGrant, CapabilityError> checked before mount; mismatches fail loudly with a typed reason.
requirements.unlocks: Third-party / dynamically-registered skins built against a contract are rejected cleanly when the host or profile can't satisfy them, instead of panicking at render.
requirements.doctrinal_note: Negotiation is a host responsibility. The closed intent enum is non_exhaustive, so a manifest names intents by stable IntentId to survive enum growth.

requirements.title: Persona/permission gate at the dispatcher, keyed by intent ORIGIN
requirements.principle: Every interaction is observable, governed, and replayable
requirements.shape: SkinContext.permissions:Permissions { persona:Persona (Author|Reviewer|ReadOnly), can_mutate:bool, allowed_intents:IntentMask }; dispatcher rejects disallowed intents with IntentReceipt { error:Forbidden{persona} }. Gate evaluates PER INTENT ORIGIN (local session or peer_id), not a single session persona. SelectNode/Recalculate/SetNote may stay allowed for Reviewer.
requirements.unlocks: Reviewer/commenter mode enforced centrally; shared review workflows; and the per-peer gating that collaboration requires (a reviewer peer's remote intents gated at the SAME dispatcher).
requirements.doctrinal_note: CRITIQUE FIX (2-major): made the gate per-intent-ORIGIN so it serves both single-user reviewer mode AND collaboration's per-peer permission (which the open_questions flagged as unspecified). Permission MUST gate at the dispatcher chokepoint, never in skin code. Forbidden is a typed IntentError variant.

requirements.title: Recordable intent + receipt + delta log with deterministic replay
requirements.principle: Every interaction is observable, governed, and replayable
requirements.shape: IntentRecorder taps the dispatcher: append (seq, intent, receipt, delta, value_epoch, persona, origin); replay(log, fresh_workspace)->WorkspaceState; serializable fixtures; WorkspaceState may expose recent_intents summary.
requirements.unlocks: Deterministic skin tests against recorded sessions; reproducible bug reports; time-travel debugging; auditable who-changed-what; the wire format for collaboration.
requirements.doctrinal_note: The intent stream is the host's behavioral surface; recording is a host concern. Replay re-issues intents through the SAME dispatcher (not inverse-undo, not bypassing the engine), requiring stable NodeKey and the host being the sole mutation path.

requirements.title: Per-slot skin panic/error isolation boundary
requirements.principle: The frame is composable, negotiated, and presentation-tokened
requirements.shape: Shell wraps each slot mount in an error boundary; a panicking/erroring skin shows a fallback in ITS slot and is unmounted/restartable without taking down other slots or the host.
requirements.unlocks: A buggy third-party skin in the inspector pane can't crash the whole workspace; the tree keeps working.
requirements.doctrinal_note: Isolation is a shell/host composition responsibility — the host owns the mount lifecycle and must contain faults at the slot boundary.

requirements.title: Empty-state / starter-template seeding + onboarding metadata
requirements.principle: The frame is composable, negotiated, and presentation-tokened
requirements.shape: NewWorkspace optionally seeds from a named StarterTemplate via template-subsystem; the command catalog exposes help-text/onboarding metadata; an empty workspace projects a guided empty-state hint.
requirements.unlocks: A guided first-run for non-core authors and Excel-migrants; sample models; discoverability beyond the command palette.
requirements.doctrinal_note: CRITIQUE FIX (2-minor): cold-start was silently absent for a platform pitched to non-core authors and import users. Low cost once templates land; named explicitly rather than left implicit. Acceptable to defer.

requirements.title: External/RTD value injection with host-pumped async-pending lifecycle
requirements.principle: Every interaction is observable, governed, and replayable
requirements.shape: WorkspaceIntent::UpdateExternalValue { handle, value } / ::InvalidateExternal { handle } feed an engine external-value source; affected nodes go Pending then resolve when the HOST pumps the resolving tick on its worker; NodeValueProjection gains External provenance.
requirements.unlocks: Live external feeds (RTD-style market data, sensor streams) drive recalc without the host blocking; skins show pending then live values.
requirements.doctrinal_note: CRITIQUE FIX (1-major, 3-major): external value SOURCES + invalidation are engine truth (they join the dependency graph + epochs), but the engine stays SYNCHRONOUS — the host pumps the resolving tick on its worker (model A). 'Passive-engine preserved' is now literally true because the engine does not compute on its own thread. The external-source intake is the new-capability part.

requirements.title: Collaboration: typed conflict resolution over the revision DAG
requirements.principle: Every interaction is observable, governed, and replayable
requirements.shape: enum ConflictResolution { Rebase, Reject, Merge }; OxCalc reports a typed ConflictReport when two peers' intents target overlapping nodes against the same basis revision; resolution policy lives in the immutable revision graph.
requirements.unlocks: The keystone of any multi-user story: detecting and resolving overlapping concurrent edits deterministically instead of a doctrinal hand-wave.
requirements.doctrinal_note: CRITIQUE FIX (2-major/strongest): the single collab requirement deferred the ONE hard part (conflict policy) to a hand-wave. Promoted to a named requirement; conflict detection/resolution + revision ordering are engine truth. This is a research-grade workstream — see research bucket caveat in open_questions.

requirements.title: Collaboration: rebase a remote intent from its basis onto local head
requirements.principle: All-or-nothing, reversible only by navigation
requirements.shape: OxCalc rebase(intent, from_basis:RevisionId, onto_head:RevisionId)->RebasedIntent|Conflict; structural edits keyed on NodeKey rebase tractably; content/formula edits and collection membership may conflict.
requirements.unlocks: A remote intent authored against revision R re-applies against local head R' — the mechanical core of co-editing.
requirements.doctrinal_note: CRITIQUE FIX (2-major): rebase was an unaddressed sub-domain. NodeKey-keyed structural rebase is tractable; content rebase is not free — this is genuinely research-grade and gated behind conflict-policy.

requirements.title: Collaboration: presence + edit-claim soft-lock markers
requirements.principle: The frame is composable, negotiated, and presentation-tokened
requirements.shape: Shared state gains peers:Vec<PresenceMarker { peer_id, slot, selection:NodeKey, editing:Option<NodeKey> }>; WorkspaceIntent::ClaimNode/ReleaseNode advisory soft-locks surfaced in projection.
requirements.unlocks: Live presence cursors, who-is-editing-which-node, and advisory claims preventing two users editing the same formula.
requirements.doctrinal_note: CRITIQUE FIX (2-major): presence beyond a cursor (claims/soft-locks) was missing. Markers are view-coordination in host shared state; claims are advisory host intents. Conflict semantics stay out of skins entirely.

matrix.skin_ir: NodeView { key:NodeKey, display_path } (transition window carries both); all maps/selection/state use NodeKey; ValueProvenance per value
matrix.host_projection: derive display_path from key; map engine invalidation to deltas; identity-keyed SkinState gc
matrix.host_intent: selection/scope/clipboard/log key on NodeKey; receipt joins intent->revision via txn id
matrix.oxcalc: engine ALREADY mints stable TreeNodeId (expose-existing); per-node value epoch is extend-existing engine bookkeeping; resolution map handle->NodeKey

matrix.skin_ir: InvalidationReason/DependencyKind/CarrierDetail/BindingDiagnostic enums; PhaseKey-keyed timing map with Other(String); richer NodeValueProjection; closed run/calc_state
matrix.host_projection: runtime_effects list, overlay_deltas, full derivation_traces, active-node-detail; per-edge cache CONTINGENT on engine exposing per-edge outcomes
matrix.oxcalc: expose existing invalidation/scheduling/overlay records verbatim; commit to PhaseKey enum; RETIRE control-flow-via-diagnostic-string; cycle iteration only fixture-surfaced today (extend)
matrix.oxfml: expose prepared-call tree + hole bindings; emit typed bind diagnostics; expose evaluated CF results

matrix.skin_ir: NodeValueProjection typed variants incl. Rich/Image + UnitHint; FormattedValue/EffectiveFormat shapes

waves.wave: W0 — Identity keystone + free typed-vs-stringly conversions
waves.theme: NodeKey first and ALONE; then the independent zero-risk typing conversions
waves.rationale: CRITIQUE FIX (3-minor): only stable-node-identity is a true universal precondition (depends_on:[]) — it gates delta addressing, persistence gc, selection survival, history correlation. Land it via a TRANSITION WINDOW (carry both key+path), not a big-bang cutover, to de-risk the keystone. The typed conversions are independent, parallelizable, low-risk expose-existing/extend work that can land in ANY order — framed as 'free, do anytime' rather than strictly sequenced. NOTE: value-epoch-keying is deliberately MOVED OUT of W0 (it is engine bookkeeping, not a free thread-through) and phase-timings/typed-run carry small engine obligations.
waves.unlocks: Skins correlate facts across recalcs and structural edits; reason chips, dependency-kind filters, typed value rendering; the IR stops lying about what it knows AND the engine stops branching on its own prose.

waves.theme: Render values as Excel would; surface the derivation the engine already holds
waves.rationale: With typed values present, the resolver (a thin OxFml forward, NOT a host reimplementation) + effective format close constraint-9; reference-resolution + binding diagnostics power navigation and inline feedback; runtime/derivation/cycle surfaces turn the X-ray on. value-epoch-keying lands here as honest engine bookkeeping (extend-existing) rather than a W0 freebie. per-edge-cache and typed-cycle are honestly extend-existing pending engine confirmation.
waves.unlocks: Excel-faithful value display everywhere; FLOW's explain-stack, calc X-ray (effects/cycle lanes), formula bar with live binding diagnostics, jump-to-definition / find-references; per-node value epochs for downstream memo/diff.

waves.wave: W2 — Subjects, transactions, typed errors & safe structural authoring
waves.theme: First-class subjects + atomic publish-once + typed failure + foresight, standing on W0/W1 alone
waves.rationale: CRITIQUE FIX (3-blocking/major, 2-major): transaction-scope is the highest-RISK foundational item (the engine publishes per-node today — accumulate-publish-once is genuine rework). typed-intent-error closes a tenet-2 violation hiding in the receipt and is sequenced HERE, not deferred. The legality/plan preview is a thin host JOIN over engine dry_bind + plan_invalidation; recalc-plan-preview reads the COMMITTED graph and does NOT back-edge into the candidate substrate, so this wave stands on W0/W1 only — the W2->W4 inversion is broken. drag-gesture and model-query are the added tree-platform domains.
waves.unlocks: Confident structural editing: batch select-and-act, atomic multi-edit, recoverable typed rejections, pre-commit 'this rebinds 7 dependents', live drop-validity, model search, command-palette enablement, reorganize the tree without breaking formulas.

waves.theme: Fill, F4, point-mode insert, paste, duplicate, set-membership, meta/notes — all id/handle-carrying
waves.rationale: The authoring verbs that compose RAW text in OxFml and rebind in OxCalc — each carries ids/handles/scope, never skin-synthesized text (constraint 1); reference-insertion COMPOSES text the HOST splices (caret stays host-side). They depend on scope+transaction from W2 and reference-resolution from W1. paste-special and duplicate-subtree are retagged L (they reuse the same hard rebind machinery as replicate-by-id, not cheaper). format-write feeds the resolver already in place.
waves.unlocks: Excel-parity fill-down/right, F4 cycling, point-mode reference insertion, paste-special, subtree duplication, authored reference collections, meta subtrees, notes, number formats — the deliberate write surface.

waves.theme: Build the retained navigable revision DAG the entire time axis depends on
waves.rationale: CRITIQUE FIX (3-blocking): the engine holds snapshot-IDENTITY hashes, NOT a retained navigable revision store ('retained non-table replay missing'). Undo-by-navigation has NO substrate today. This is an explicit gating engine milestone that MUST precede the time axis and collaboration — isolated into its own sub-wave so its risk is visible and not buried among IR shapes.
waves.unlocks: The substrate for undo-navigation, version-history, time-scrubbing, and (later) collaboration — nothing in the time axis is schedulable before this lands.

waves.wave: W4b — Candidate substrate (gating engine workstream) + time axis
waves.theme: Build the addressable candidate-overlay substrate, then provenance, undo & history on top
waves.rationale: CRITIQUE FIX (3-blocking/strongest): candidate-overlay-handle is the single LARGEST engine risk — the engine has a per-node publish lifecycle + a SINGLE overlay set, NOT N addressable layerable non-publishing contexts; this is NEW-CAPABILITY, not extend-existing, and gates the whole speculation band. Sequenced as a milestone with provenance + commit/discard. undo/history ride on W4a's revision graph (also new-capability). value-shape-diff inherits value-epoch-keying's risk.
waves.unlocks: Consequence-free what-if substrate; ghost-vs-real provenance; commit-to-history bridge; deterministic undo by navigation; branchable DAG history; the delta-ledger change-pulse.

waves.theme: The author-facing speculation features riding the proven candidate substrate
waves.rationale: With the candidate substrate proven in W4b, the scenario rail, ghost preview, comparison columns, and chart-feed series-projection are buildable. Kept distinct from W4b so they do not appear schedulable before the substrate exists.
waves.unlocks: FLOW's ghost what-if, scenario rail (Base/Bull/Bear comparison columns), comparative projection, and chart-ready series feeds — explore freely, commit deliberately.

waves.wave: W5 — Platform robustness: deltas, host-worker async, composition, persistence, governance
waves.theme: Incremental updates, host-side concurrency, multi-pane, theming/a11y/keybinding, negotiation, observability
waves.rationale: CRITIQUE FIX (1-major, 3-major): host-worker-calc resolves the async-vs-passive contradiction by keeping the engine SYNCHRONOUS and making concurrency a HOST concern (engine n/a) — so 'host drives every tick' holds literally. The delta channel keys on the engine's existing invalidated-node set (NOT blocked by per-node value epochs). multi-slot + focus + keybinding + isolation + tokens + a11y + manifest deliver the composable frame; persona gates per ORIGIN (serving collab too); frame-telemetry makes the perf goal falsifiable; audited-shared-state treats recalc_mode as dispatcher policy.
waves.unlocks: 60fps on 100k-node models with measurable frame budget; the full FLOW multi-pane layout; dark/high-contrast/RTL themable accessible skins; arbitrated keybindings; third-party + reviewer extensibility; deterministic replayable tests; persistent view-state.

waves.rationale: Reach-extending capabilities on every prior wave: templates/tables/aliases/import/export are structural-reuse and the canonical-verification round-trip; batch-repair completes the rejection lifecycle; goal-seek/sweep + RTD are gated behind the proven candidate (W4b) and host-worker (W5) milestones rather than listed as independently schedulable; onboarding seeds from templates.

This prevents the matrix diluting into a wishlist.

Per-node published-value epoch: confirm the engine can stamp each node's PUBLISHED value with an epoch distinct from the per-node INPUT epoch. If only a workspace value_epoch + per-node input_epoch exist, value-epoch-keying and value-shape-diff are materially larger than tagged; the delta channel is already decoupled (keys on the invalidated-node set) but skin memoization and per-node staleness still want true per-node value epochs.

Candidate-overlay reach: candidate-overlay-handle is now tagged NEW-CAPABILITY, but the SIZE of the scheduler rework to go from one per-node publish path + single overlay set to N addressable, layerable (parented), non-publishing contexts is unestimated and is the single largest risk gating the entire speculation band. Needs an engine spike before W4b is schedulable.

Retained revision graph: revision-graph-retention is now an explicit gating milestone, but the engine today holds only snapshot-IDENTITY hashes ('retained non-table replay missing'). Confirm whether a navigable parent-linked revision store with a cursor is a bounded extension of the existing snapshot machinery or a from-scratch store with its own memory/GC budget.

Passivity model is committed to (A) — engine single-threaded, host owns the worker and pumps bounded calc slices. Confirm the engine's synchronous calc can be sliced/resumed cooperatively (so the host can pump it without blocking a frame), or whether bounded-slice pumping itself requires engine reentrancy work.

Per-edge cache outcomes: confirm the scheduler exposes per-edge Hit/Miss/Bypassed, or only an edge-value-cache BASIS fingerprint. per-edge-cache-evidence is tagged extend-existing pending this; if only the basis exists, the per-edge report is new bookkeeping.

General iterative-convergence engine: confirm whether OxCalc has a general iterative solver producing per-iteration max_change for arbitrary cycles, or only Excel-match cycle FIXTURES. typed-cycle-diagnostics (extend-existing) and goal-seek-substrate (new-capability) both depend on the answer.

Delta-channel vs full-republish contract: the delta is additive (alongside the full snapshot) today. At 100k nodes skins will want delta-ONLY. Is the synchronous full-republish guarantee mandatory forever, or is there a sanctioned mode where the full snapshot is sent only on resync/gap (projection-version-stamp triggers it)?

Table as node-rooted structured value vs grid: table-structural-ops and table-cell-readback walk close to constraint 3. Is there an existing engine notion of 'table' that reconciles rows AND columns without reintroducing 2D coordinate addressing, or does treating a table as anything with both dimensions risk back-dooring A1-range semantics?

Durable scenario store: scenario-persist-migrate keeps names in SkinState and override VALUES in the engine model. Does the engine model have a durable, Excel-round-tripping place for named scenario overrides (scenario-manager parity), or do override values live only in transient runtime overlays — in which case durability is itself a new engine capability, not n/a.

Collaboration is now an explicit RESEARCH bucket (W7), off the roadmap. Before it can be planned: which conflict model (rebase over the revision DAG vs reject vs merge) does the immutable-revision substrate naturally support, and does NodeKey-keyed structural rebase compose with content/formula and collection-membership rebase without a separate merge algebra?

Persona source of truth for the per-ORIGIN dispatcher gate: does the persona come from host config, the capability-manifest negotiation, or an external auth layer — and for remote peer intents (W7), how is the originating peer's persona authenticated at the single dispatcher chokepoint?
